title: How Can You Use Inito in Your Follicular Phase?
summary: Learn how to use Inito in your follicular phase to identify your fertile window, track hormone changes, log fertility data, and better understand your cycle.
body_text: Your follicular phase is where a new cycle (and a new chance to conceive) begins. While your body is busy preparing for ovulation, your hormone levels are constantly changing behind the scenes. With Inito, you can follow these changes in real time to better understand your fertile window, recognize your unique patterns, and make more informed decisions throughout your cycle. Disclaimer: Inito is intended for tracking your fertile window and confirming ovulation. It is not designed to diagnose medical conditions, detect or track pregnancy, or replace medical advice. Key Takeaways Follicular phase starts on the first day of your period and ends with ovulation. It’s the most variable part of the menstrual cycle since ovulation may not happen on the same day every month. Tracking estrogen during your follicular phase can help identify your right fertile days. Tracking beta-LH helps capture your unique LH pattern instead of relying only on fixed thresholds, and helps reduce cross-reactivity seen with some traditional ovulation tests. Comparing hormone trends across multiple cycles can help you learn what’s typical for your body and spot meaningful changes over time. Logging symptoms alongside your hormone data can help you identify patterns leading up to ovulation and better understand your cycle. You can also keep important fertility information, such as blood test results, follicle scans, medications, and IUI details, in one place in the Inito app. If you notice persistent changes like highly irregular cycles, repeated delayed ovulation, or no clear LH surge across multiple cycles, it’s a good idea to discuss them with your healthcare provider. What is the follicular phase? The follicular phase is the first part of your menstrual cycle. It begins on the first day of your bleed and goes on until you ovulate. During this time, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) encourages several follicles in your ovaries to grow. As one follicle becomes dominant, it produces increasing amounts of estrogen, preparing your body for egg release. Unlike the luteal phase , which is relatively consistent at around 12-14 days, the follicular phase can vary significantly from cycle to cycle. In a study of more than 600,000 menstrual cycles, the average follicular phase lasted 16.9 days , with many healthy cycles falling anywhere between 11.6 and 22.2 days. Know more: Trying to Get Pregnant? Get to Know Your Follicular Phase What hormones does Inito track during the follicular phase? Inito measures 4 fertility hormones in urine during your follicular phase as well as throughout the cycle: FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone), LH (luteinizing hormone), E3G (estrogen), and PdG (urine metabolite of progesterone). FSH (follicle stimulating hormone): Supports follicle growth early in the cycle. E3G (urine metabolite of estrogen): Estrogen starts rising as follicles mature, peaking about 3-4 days before ovulation. Inito uses this rise from your baseline to identify your High Fertility days. LH (luteinizing hormone): Surges shortly before ovulation and signals that the egg is likely to be released within the next 24-36 hours. Inito identifies a rise in your LH from your baseline to give you Peak Fertility. PdG (urine metabolite of progesterone): PdG becomes more relevant after ovulation and helps confirm if ovulation has actually occurred. How Can You Use Inito in Your Follicular Phase? Here’s how you can use Inito to make the most of your follicular phase: Track your estrogen rise and identify High Fertility days to recognize your right days to try. Monitor your LH surge and Peak Fertility to better time intercourse/ insemination. Understand cycle-to-cycle variation by comparing hormone trends across multiple cycles. Better understand the relationship between hormone fluctuations and symptoms across the cycle. Keep all your fertility information in one place and see it alongside your hormone trends by logging your blood test results, follicle scans, medications, trigger shots, or IUI details on the Inito app. Let’s take a look at each of these in detail. How does Inito detect High Fertility? Inito detects High Fertility by identifying when your estrogen (E3G) levels begin to rise from your baseline. As your follicles mature, estrogen typically increases around 3-4 days before the LH surge. It’s one of the earliest signs that ovulation is approaching. Why this matters Sperm can typically survive in the female body for up to five days. That means having intercourse before ovulation can improve your chances of conception . In fact, having sex before ovulation leads to the highest chances of pregnancy! Know more: When to Have Sex to Conceive This is important because many couples mistime intercourse . In one study, although over two-thirds of women believed they were trying during their fertile window, only 12.7% accurately identified it . So, by tracking real-time hormone changes rather than calendar estimates, Inito helps recognize the right days to try and plan accordingly. Why should you track your LH surge? LH rises shortly before ovulation and typically signals that ovulation is likely within the next 24-36 hours. Identifying this surge helps narrow down your most fertile days and can improve timing for intercourse or insemination. However, LH patterns are often more complex than many people realize. Research shows that not everyone experiences a single sharp surge. Approximately 48% of women have one distinct LH surge , while others experience other types of LH surge patterns, like plateau surges, biphasic surges, or multiple LH rises before ovulation . Know more: What Does a Normal LH Level Look Like? Additionally, LH concentrations during a surge vary widely between individuals. In one study, ovulation occurred across a broad range of LH values–from around 6.5 mIU/mL to over 100 mIU/mL –meaning there is no “universal” threshold that applies to everyone. However, traditional ovulation predictor kits often rely on population averages and commonly detect alpha-LH, which may be more susceptible to cross-reactivity. Inito measures beta-LH and gives you results based on your unique baseline, providing a more personalized picture of your LH pattern and cycle trends. Know more: How Accurate Are Ovulation Tests? Can tracking multiple cycles help you understand your body better? Yes. One of the biggest advantages of hormone tracking is recognizing trends over time rather than focusing on a single cycle. Your follicular phase may naturally vary from cycle to cycle. You might notice: Earlier or later estrogen rises Longer or shorter follicular phases Multiple LH surges before ovulation Delayed ovulation in some cycles For example, in the charts above, the same user has 2 different hormone patterns. ( Note : The charts in this article are recreated for illustration purposes. They are based on real hormone patterns to help explain different scenarios and are not actual user charts.) In their first chart, we see that her estrogen levels rose above baseline on CD 9, she had one LH surge on CD 12, and then another one on CD 14. This is a biphasic LH surge pattern, where LH rises, goes down the next day, and then rises again the day after that. This may be because sometimes the first LH surge isn’t enough to trigger ovulation, so the body may try again with a second surge. It’s seen in about 44% of women . We know ovulation occurred, since there was a steady and consistent rise in PdG after the second LH surge. Now, let’s take a look at her second chart: We can see that their estrogen started rising from CD 11 onwards. She saw a single LH surge on CD 14, and ovulation was confirmed on CD 18. Variations like these are more common than you think. Many everyday factors, including stress, travel, illness, sleep disruptions, and lifestyle changes, can temporarily affect ovulation timing. Looking at multiple cycles together helps distinguish occasional variation from recurring patterns and gives you a better understanding of what is typical for your own body. Know more: What Your Hormone Chart Reveals About Your Cycle How can symptom tracking complement hormone tracking? Hormones influence more than fertility: they often affect how you feel throughout the follicular phase. You may notice changes in: Energy levels Cervical mucus Mood and motivation Libido Exercise performance Recording these observations alongside hormone trends can help you recognize recurring patterns before ovulation. Over time, this combined information may make it easier to anticipate your fertile window and understand how hormonal changes affect your daily life. And if you’re curious about aligning your exercise or nutrition with different stages of your cycle, you may also want to explore concepts like cycle syncing. Know more: Cycle Syncing: What it Is and How to Start What if your follicular phase looks different from previous cycles? Variation from one cycle to another is common, especially in the follicular phase. However, you may want to pay closer attention if you consistently notice: Very short or very long menstrual cycles (<21 days or >35 days) Highly irregular cycle lengths No LH surge across multiple cycles No ovulation confirmation over several cycles Symptoms that interfere with your daily activities These patterns do not automatically indicate that something is wrong. However, if they persist (especially when you’re trying to conceive), they can provide useful information to discuss with your healthcare provider. What should you do during your follicular phase? Beyond tracking hormones, supporting your overall health can help you feel your best during the follicular phase! Here are some other things worth paying attention to: Nutrition A balanced eating pattern that includes whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, fruits, and vegetables can do wonders. Many people also choose foods that support overall hormonal health and estrogen metabolism, like high-fiber, plant-based, and whole foods. Know more: The Best Follicular Phase Foods To Eat Exercise Many people report feeling more energetic and motivated during this stage of the cycle. If that sounds like you, this can be a great time for higher-intensity workouts or strength training (while still listening to your body’s needs, of course!). Social activities and productivity Due to rising estrogen levels, you might be seeing improvements in mood, confidence, or motivation during the follicular phase. This makes it a good time for collaborative projects or social engagements. Community support Trying to conceive is different for everyone, and it can sometimes feel like you’re navigating more questions than answers. Connecting with others who are on a similar journey can make it feel a little less overwhelming. If you’re looking for a place to learn, share experiences, and find support, we’d love to have you in the Inito Community ! What can Inito help you track during the follicular phase? To sum it up, here’s how you can use Inito during your follicular phase: What you’re tracking Why it matters Estrogen rise and High Fertility days Identifies the beginning of your fertile window so you can start trying. LH surge Helps detect your individual LH pattern and identify Peak Fertility without relying solely on fixed thresholds and minimizing the chances of false positives. Cycle-to-cycle variation Reveals how your follicular phase changes over time and what is typical for your body. Hormone trends and symptoms Combines objective hormone data with personal observations to better understand your cycle. The Bottom Line Your follicular phase is when your body prepares for ovulation, making it one of the most informative times to track your hormones if you’re trying to conceive. By monitoring estrogen, LH, FSH, and PdG, Inito helps you see the bigger picture of your cycle: not just whether you’re about to ovulate, but how your hormones change throughout the cycle. Whether you’re identifying your fertile window, learning your unique LH pattern, or understanding how your cycles vary over time, consistent hormone tracking can help you better understand your fertility. FAQs What hormones does Inito measure during the follicular phase? Inito measures four key fertility hormones during the follicular phase as well as throughout your cycle: LH, estrogen, PdG, and FSH. During the follicular phase, estrogen, LH, and FSH are especially important for tracking follicle development and identifying your fertile window. Can Inito predict ovulation before an LH surge? Kind of. Inito tracks rising estrogen, which typically increases 3-4 days before your LH surge. This helps identify the start of your fertile window before ovulation is expected. Why is my follicular phase longer this month? Don’t worry, this is more common than you think! The follicular phase is the most variable part of the menstrual cycle, so it’s normal for its length to change from one cycle to the next. Things like stress, illness, travel, sleep, and natural biological variation can all affect when you ovulate. Can I have more than one LH surge? Yes! Not everyone has the classic single LH peak. You may see a double surge or even multiple LH surges before ovulation. That’s why it’s more helpful to look at your hormone trends rather than relying on a single positive ovulation test. Should I use Inito during my period? Yes, you can. Inito recommends testing from CD (cycle day) 6 onwards. This helps establish your baseline hormone levels early in the cycle, making it easier to detect meaningful hormone changes as your fertile window approaches. If your reference day test overlaps with your period, it’s totally okay to test! Just make sure you’re using a tampon or menstrual cup to avoid blood mixing with your urine and altering your results. What else can I track in the Inito app? Along with hormone testing, you can log symptoms, blood test results, follicle scans, fertility medications, trigger shots, insemination details, pregnancy tests, and other cycle information to keep everything in one place.

Oracle Expands Powerful AI Capabilities in Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud to Supercharge Enterprise Data Innovation
summary: Oracle is introducing Oracle AI Database Agent for Gemini Enterprise, enabling Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud customers to ask questions of their Oracle data using natural language—no SQL required. Learn more about how Oracle and Google Cloud are expanding their partnership.
body_text: Oracle has expanded its partnership with Google Cloud to give joint customers new ways to operationalize AI across enterprise data. Under the expanded partnership, the Oracle AI Database Agent for Gemini Enterprise gives Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud customers a simpler way to interact with their Oracle data using natural language. In addition, Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud now offers new capabilities and broader regional availability as global organizations, such as Worldline, use it to drive innovation and accelerate cloud migrations. “We’re making it easier for customers to use natural language to access, understand, and act on enterprise data by combining the Gemini Enterprise experience with Oracle’s industry-leading database performance, security, and governance,” said Nathan Thomas, senior vice president, product management, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. “By applying AI directly to enterprise data at the database layer, customers can improve accuracy, strengthen controls, and use models more efficiently without exposing sensitive data or adding complexity. Together, we’re making it easier for our customers to power agentic AI with trusted business data.” “To deliver real impact from agentic AI, customers need a simple, trusted way to interact with their valuable business data using intelligent agents such as the Oracle AI Database Agent,” said Satish Thomas, vice president, applied AI & platform ecosystem, Google Cloud. “By making this agent accessible through Gemini Enterprise, we’re giving customers greater flexibility to apply AI to data stored in Oracle databases and turn that data into meaningful business value.” The Oracle AI Database Agent, now available in the Google Cloud Marketplace , allows Gemini Enterprise customers to use natural language when interacting with their trusted Oracle data, while drawing on the in-database AI capabilities of Oracle AI Database to deliver relevant, context-aware answers. Customers can ask everyday business questions—such as analyzing revenue trends across regions and product lines—and receive immediate, data-driven answers that help them adjust pricing or prioritize sales efforts, all without writing SQL or building custom tools. The agent interprets each request, queries relevant, governed Oracle data, and delivers clear insights without moving or duplicating data. In addition, the Oracle AI Database Agent enables developers to securely use Oracle data in more advanced AI workflows by allowing them to connect it with other AI tools in Google’s Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform to automate tasks such as data extraction, analysis, and visualization. AI Shift is a CyberAgent subsidiary that helps enterprises in Japan build and deploy agentic AI solutions to automate business processes across customer service, marketing, and sales. AI Shift uses Oracle Autonomous AI Database on OCI to power its agent development platform and plans to use Oracle AI Database Agent to help customers expand their Oracle AI Database deployments to Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud. “The Oracle AI Database Agent represents an important advancement in how we use AI with enterprise data,” said Yuto Yoneyama, CEO, AI Shift. “With Gemini Enterprise, our users can move from writing SQL to asking questions in natural language to get answers grounded in trusted enterprise data. That helps us speed development, improve the quality of results, and make faster, more informed decisions without compromising governance and control.” Leading Organizations Choose Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud Global organizations, such as Worldline, are adopting Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud to accelerate their cloud migrations. Worldline is a European payments provider that processes billions of transactions globally. To support its strict requirements for performance and security, Worldline is leveraging Oracle Exadata Database Service on Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud to modernize its payment processing platform and deliver scalable, low-latency, and secure payment services. “Worldline operates one of the largest payment processing platforms, for which consistent low latency and high throughput are non-negotiable,” said Arni Smit, director, software engineering, integration and payment platform, Worldline. “Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud gives us the scalability, resilience, and security capabilities we require to support real-time transaction processing at global scale by delivering the power of Oracle Exadata within Google Cloud.” New Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud Capabilities and Regions New database capabilities and additional regions are supporting growing demand from across the world by providing customers with more options and locations to use Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) GoldenGate enables real-time Oracle database migration: Enables customers to simplify migrations of Oracle databases to Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud and implement high-availability solutions through real-time, low-impact data movement. In addition, the service integrates with Google BigQuery for near real-time analytics, eliminating latency between operational and analytical systems. Generally available soon, OCI GoldenGate enables customers to act on live data without building complex data pipelines. Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse integration with Google BigQuery: Enables customers to seamlessly access and analyze open-format data stored in Google Cloud Lakehouse by allowing Oracle Autonomous AI Lakehouse to directly read BigQuery Iceberg tables without data duplication. This helps customers build a unified lakehouse architecture that supports analytics and AI workloads across Oracle and Google Cloud while reducing data movement and associated costs. Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud new region availability: Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud is now available in 15 regions: Asia-Northeast 1 (Tokyo), Asia-Northeast 2 (Osaka), Asia-South 1 (Mumbai), Asia-South 2 (Delhi), Australia-Southeast 1 (Sydney), Australia-Southeast 2 (Melbourne), Europe-West 8 (Milan), Germany Central (Frankfurt), North America-Northeast 1 (Montreal), North America-Northeast 2 (Toronto), South America-East 1 (São Paulo), UK South (London), US Central 1 (Iowa), US East (Ashburn), and US West (Salt Lake City). To support growing customer demand, additional regional availability is planned within the next 12 months in Europe-West 12 (Turin) and North America-South 1 (Mexico). Proving neglect, abuse, or facility misconduct requires documenting patterns over extended timeframes, often months or years of care, across multiple providers and facility types. The Role of Medical Records in Proving Elder Abuse Medical records serve as the foundation for elder abuse claims in several critical ways: documenting physical indicators such as pressure ulcers, malnutrition, dehydration, unexplained injuries, and medication errors; establishing timelines showing when symptoms appeared and how they progressed under facility care; proving causation by linking facility negligence to patient harm through treatment gaps and missed interventions; and calculating damages through billing records and documented suffering. Elder abuse litigation generally requires substantial documentation showing a pattern of neglect rather than isolated incidents. This means attorneys must gather records from nursing homes, hospitals, specialists, pharmacies, and emergency services to build a complete picture. Challenges in Obtaining Records for Vulnerable Adults Several factors complicate medical record retrieval for elder abuse cases: patients often move between nursing homes, rehabilitation centers, and hospitals; clients may have cognitive impairment that limits their ability to recall treatment locations or sign authorizations; nursing homes facing liability may delay or obstruct records access; deceased patient records require estate representative authorization with death certificates; and long-term care generates thousands of pages requiring systematic organization. Speeding Up Case Preparation: How Fast Medical Record Retrieval Benefits Elder Abuse Claims Traditional manual retrieval processes commonly take a month or more, an unwelcome timeline when statute of limitations deadlines approach or family members need answers about a loved one's care. Traditional Retrieval vs. Accelerated Services Manual retrieval carries real limitations: phone and fax follow-ups consume significant staff time, incomplete authorizations restart part of the retrieval clock, there's little visibility into provider response status, and records often arrive disorganized, requiring additional sorting time. AI-accelerated retrieval offers real advantages instead: automated daily provider follow-ups maintain consistent pressure, pre-submission error detection helps prevent rejection delays, real-time status tracking eliminates guesswork, and organized chronological delivery reduces review time. Codes Health works toward delivering medical records in a couple of weeks by combining AI-powered request validation with persistent operational follow-up. The platform automatically flags misspellings, missing dates, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections. A note about same-day retrieval services: Codes Health's position is that some competitors advertising same-day or expedited turnaround often deliver incomplete records that require ongoing client involvement to resolve gaps, an experience that can contribute to higher client churn and further delay. Codes Health instead prioritizes completeness, working toward comprehensive records in a couple of weeks rather than months. Impact of Timely Records on Case Outcomes Speed can meaningfully affect elder abuse case outcomes: complete records enable quicker expert witness review and opinion development, organized evidence packages demonstrate case preparation quality during settlement talks, earlier retrieval helps preserve evidence before facility closures or storage-policy losses, and expedited answers can offer some resolution for grieving families. Beyond Documents: AI-Powered Analysis for Elder Abuse Evidence Modern retrieval platforms do more than obtain records; they can analyze them for case-critical insights that might otherwise stay buried across thousands of pages. Identifying Red Flags with Advanced Data Processing AI-powered analysis can help identify patterns human reviewers might miss, including repeated injuries such as falls, bruises, or fractures documented across multiple encounters, medication discrepancies where prescriptions contradict or duplicate existing medications, weight loss trends indicating progressive malnutrition, incident clustering during specific shifts or staffing levels, and documentation gaps where assessments or care plans are missing during critical periods. General AI platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record analysis and are not a reliable substitute for a purpose-built tool. Codes Health uses legal-grade AI trained for personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice cases, built to handle the nuances that matter for litigation with high precision. Building Comprehensive Timelines of Care AI-generated chronologies transform scattered records into more usable case narratives: records get sorted chronologically across all providers, potential care standard violations get flagged for attorney review, documented conditions surface without manual searching, and treatment recommendations supporting future-expense damages calculations get identified. Ensuring Complete Records: Why 'Missing Records Review' Matters Incomplete records create real risk in elder abuse litigation. Missing incident reports and documentation gaps can appear in cases that rely on basic retrieval services, undermining a case at trial or during settlement negotiations. The Dangers of Incomplete Medical Histories Incomplete records create several risks: missing treatment notes leave gaps in the injury timeline that weaken causation arguments, providers may produce records at deposition that undermine your narrative, insurance adjusters may discount claims with obvious documentation holes, and medical experts cannot render complete opinions without complete records. Methods for Verifying Record Completeness Codes Health's Missing Record Review compares returned materials against the original request and known treatment history, using facility gap analysis to identify providers mentioned in records but not yet requested, date range verification to confirm requested timeframes are represented, record type checking to ensure billing records, imaging, and nursing notes are all included, and resolution before delivery by working with facilities to obtain missing documents before closing requests. Streamlined Process: How Integration Enhances Medical Record Retrieval for Law Firms Managing dozens of provider requests across multiple elder abuse cases creates administrative burden without proper systems. Context-switching between case management software, retrieval vendor portals, email, and downloaded files wastes time and creates errors, so keeping everything in one place matters. Filevine users can submit requests from the relevant case file, track status in real time without leaving the platform, communicate with the Codes Health team within the case workflow, and receive completed records and billing inside the Filevine project. The integration validates authorizations and requirements before submission, manages follow-up across calls, faxes, emails, and portals, and verifies completeness before delivery. Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can force a resubmission and restart part of your retrieval timeline. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections. For high-volume customers, Codes Health can also build custom integrations with other CRM platforms and medical software systems. Protecting Patient Data: HIPAA-Compliant Medical Record Retrieval Elder abuse cases involve highly sensitive protected health information requiring rigorous security throughout the retrieval process. HIPAA compliance for legal teams generally requires business associate agreements with any vendor handling protected health information, a minimum-necessary standard of requesting only records needed for the matter, secure encrypted transmission and storage, and role-based access controls limiting who can view sensitive records. Codes Health operates as a HIPAA-compliant platform with e-signature workflows for secure authorization collection, encrypted document storage, SOC 2 Type II certification, and audit logging of access and activity. Comprehensive Retrieval: Accessing Medical, Billing, and Imaging Records Elder abuse cases require more than clinical notes. Complete evidence packages draw from multiple record types and sources: clinical records such as nursing notes, physician orders, treatment plans, and assessments; facility records including incident reports, staffing logs, and care conference notes; billing records supporting economic damages calculations; imaging studies documenting injuries; pharmacy records including medication administration logs and prescription histories; and regulatory records such as state inspection reports and deficiency citations. Codes Health retrieves records through multiple channels, including claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, direct provider portal access, and traditional fax, email, and phone outreach for providers lacking electronic access. From Claim to Court: Sustained Support for Elder Abuse Litigation Elder abuse cases often span years from initial claim through trial, and a retrieval partner should support the entire journey. Medical records serve different purposes at each stage: initial records help determine case viability and potential value, complete packages support demand preparation and settlement negotiations, organized records facilitate efficient discovery production, chronologies enable medical expert opinion development, and certified records with proper chain of custody support trial admissibility. Before committing to a retrieval service, it's worth asking: What is your average turnaround time for nursing home records? How do you handle facilities that resist or delay records production? Do you verify completeness before delivering records? Can your platform identify care gaps and potential negligence indicators? What security certifications do you maintain? Do you integrate with my case management software? Codes Health is trusted by hundreds of firms across personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice practice areas that frequently involve elder abuse claims. The company is backed by institutional investors including Y Combinator, Amplify Partners, and General Catalyst. Ready to Strengthen Your Elder Abuse Cases? Elder abuse victims and their families deserve attorneys equipped with complete, organized evidence. Codes Health combines AI-powered retrieval with human verification to deliver the comprehensive medical records elder abuse litigation demands in a couple of weeks rather than months, with transparent flat-fee pricing. Schedule a demonstration to see how legal-grade AI can support your elder abuse practice. Frequently Asked Questions What specific types of medical records are most important in an elder abuse case? Elder abuse cases require nursing home incident reports, facility staffing records, medication administration logs, physician orders, and nursing assessments. Billing records document services rendered, while imaging studies help prove physical injuries. Records from all treating facilities, including hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and specialists, are needed to establish the complete care timeline. How does AI improve the accuracy and speed of medical record retrieval for elder abuse claims? AI platforms can help speed up retrieval by validating authorizations before submission, maintaining regular provider follow-ups, and organizing records chronologically upon delivery. For accuracy, AI analysis can identify patterns of neglect across thousands of pages that human reviewers might miss, flagging repeated injuries, medication errors, and care gaps. Codes Health combines this AI capability with human verification to help ensure findings are accurate for legal proceedings. Can medical record retrieval services help identify hidden patterns of abuse or neglect? Yes. AI-powered analysis can surface patterns that are harder to catch in manual review, such as weight loss trends indicating malnutrition, injury clusters correlating with specific staffing levels, and documentation gaps during critical care periods. These insights can help attorneys build a case for systemic negligence rather than isolated incidents, a key element in elder abuse claims. What are the privacy considerations when sharing medical records for legal purposes? All medical record retrieval must comply with HIPAA requirements, including secure transmission, encrypted storage, and proper authorization. For deceased patients, estate representative authorization with death certificates is required. For cognitively impaired clients, guardian or power of attorney documentation may be necessary. Look for retrieval partners with SOC 2 Type II certification and business associate agreements in place. How do integrated platforms like Filevine streamline the medical record retrieval process? The Filevine partnership with Codes Health allows attorneys to submit requests, track status, communicate with retrieval specialists, and receive completed records without leaving their case file. This reduces context-switching between systems and maintains a complete audit trail within the matter. The integration also validates requests before submission to help prevent rejection delays. What is the average turnaround time for obtaining medical records relevant to elder abuse cases? Traditional manual retrieval commonly takes a month or more due to provider delays and incomplete authorizations. AI-powered platforms like Codes Health work toward reducing this to a couple of weeks through automated follow-ups, pre-submission error detection, and established provider relationships. For elder abuse cases requiring records from a larger number of providers, this time savings compounds meaningfully across a case.

title: KindlyMD Reports Third Quarter 2025 Operational and Financial Results
summary: Advanced Mission of Building Leading Bitcoin Ecosystem Through Accumulation of 5,398 Bitcoin in Treasury and Completion of Two Strategic Investments
body_text: Completed Merger with Bitcoin Treasury Company Nakamoto Advanced Mission of Building Leading Bitcoin Ecosystem Through Accumulation of 5,398 Bitcoin in Treasury and Completion of Two Strategic Investments Salt Lake City, UT, November 19, 2025 – KindlyMD, Inc. (NASDAQ: NAKA) (“KindlyMD” or “the Company”), a provider of integrated healthcare services and a Bitcoin treasury company via its subsidiary Nakamoto Holdings, Inc. (“Nakamoto”), today announced its financial and operating results for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, along with an update on its Bitcoin treasury strategy. In May 2025, KindlyMD took a major strategic leap when it announced its merger with Nakamoto and subsequently raised approximately $540 million of gross proceeds from a private placement and $200 million in convertible notes to fund the purchase of Bitcoin in furtherance of its treasury strategy. Since then, Nakamoto has successfully advanced its strategy to build a durable Bitcoin-native operating platform by accumulating and holding a significant Bitcoin treasury, allocating a portion of that treasury for strategic investments in Bitcoin-focused public companies and treasury assets, and laying the foundation to acquire recurring-revenue, cash-generating Bitcoin-related businesses that can help fund further Bitcoin accumulation and ecosystem growth. "We set clear goals—merge our companies, establish a Bitcoin treasury, and begin investing strategically—and we delivered on all three,” said David Bailey, Chairman and CEO. “We’ve executed against every goal put in place this quarter, and created a strong foundation to build a long-term Bitcoin treasury company designed to thrive through every market cycle." Q3 2025 Operational Highlights During the quarter, the Company: Completed the merger of Kindly MD, Inc. and Nakamoto, establishing Nakamoto as a wholly owned subsidiary. Executed an agreement giving the Company the right to a call option to purchase BTC Inc, a leading Bitcoin-focused media company, which has the right to acquire UTXO Management GP, LLC, a high-conviction Bitcoin focused hedge fund. This agreement creates a clear pathway to add media, advisory and financial services to Nakamoto’s Bitcoin platform. Established a $5 billion at-the-market (“ATM”) equity offering program, raising $5.6 million at an average share price of $4.15 per share, and enhancing the Company’s ability to grow its Bitcoin treasury and fund strategic initiatives. This program has only been used when accretive to the Company’s shareholders. Appointed Amanda Fabiano as Chief Operating Officer to lead execution of the Company’s strategic roadmap. Formerly Head of Mining at Galaxy and Director of Bitcoin Mining at Fidelity, Mrs. Fabiano brings a decade of experience in Bitcoin finance and capital markets that informs Nakamoto’s strategic M&A and growth initiatives. Closed two investments in Bitcoin-treasury companies: a $15 million investment in Treasury BV (“Treasury”), a Bitcoin treasury company based in the Netherlands, which marks the Company’s first investment in a foreign publicly listed Bitcoin company; and a $30 million investment in the Japanese leading Bitcoin-treasury company, Metaplanet Inc. (TSE: 3350). As of September 30, 2025, the Company had purchased a cumulative amount of 5,765 Bitcoin at a weighted average price of $118,204.88 per Bitcoin for approximately $681 million. KindlyMD has utilized 367 Bitcoin for strategic investments and held 5,398 Bitcoin as of November 12, 2025. "We believe every enduring enterprise must grow, invest, earn, and save—and we’re applying the same fundamentals through the lens of Bitcoin,” said Tyler Evans, CIO. “Our Bitcoin treasury isn’t a passive reserve. It’s a strategic tool. By selectively investing in and acquiring companies that strengthen the broader Bitcoin ecosystem and support our operating goals, we aim to compound long-term shareholder value while reinforcing the foundation of our business. As we continue to execute our strategy, we will prioritize investments in enterprises that are aligned with our long-term vision." Nakamoto allocates a portion of its Bitcoin holdings to strategic investments in Bitcoin focused companies operating in international capital markets. In addition to the two investments made during the quarter, in November 2025, the Company also invested $6 million in FUTURE Holdings AG, a Bitcoin treasury company based in Switzerland. "Our focus is on disciplined execution—integrating high-quality, cash-generating businesses into a unified Bitcoin operating platform that compounds value over time,” said Amanda Fabiano, Chief Operating Officer. “We believe our investments will expand the scope and resilience of our business, adding operating revenue, talent, and market reach that reinforces the strength of our platform. We are building the foundation necessary to translate that expected growth into sustainable returns for shareholders." As part of the Bitcoin treasury strategy, Nakamoto is also focused on acquiring Bitcoin-related businesses with recurring revenue, strong margins, and mission alignment, enabling the Company to support its long-term Bitcoin strategy with cash flow. KindlyMD intends to use earnings to support Nakamoto’s efforts to accumulate Bitcoin and reinvest in strategic opportunities. Q3 2025 Financial Summary (vs. Q3 2024) Highlights from the Company’s results for the third quarter of 2025 from its Bitcoin treasury, as well as its existing integrated healthcare services business, were as follows: Total Revenue for the third quarter of 2025 was $0.4 million compared to $0.6 million in Q3 2024, which reflects the results of the Company’s healthcare business. Total operating expenses in Q3 2025 were $10.8 million compared to $1.7 million in the third quarter of 2024, primarily driven by increased SG&A costs related to the Company’s recently launched Bitcoin strategy. Net Loss for the third quarter of 2025 was $86.0 million or $(0.42) per diluted share compared to $1.0 million or $(0.17) per diluted share in Q3 2024. Net loss was primarily driven by a $59.8 million non-cash charge related to the loss on acquisition of Nakamoto and $22.1 million non-cash charge related to an unrealized loss on digital assets. The net loss was also driven by a realized loss on digital assets of $1.4 million, resulting from Bitcoin sold to fund the Company’s investments in Metaplanet Inc. and Treasury. Enterprise Value: As of September 30, 2025, the Company’s enterprise value was $635,885,949, calculated as market capitalization of $457,053,532, adding notes payable of $203,017,500, less cash and cash equivalents of $24,185,083 Shares Issued and Outstanding: As of September 30, 2025, shares issued and outstanding were 427,152,834 and 84,502,113 prefunded warrants were outstanding. As of November 14, 2025, shares issued and outstanding were 439,850,889, and 71,704,975 prefunded warrants were outstanding. About KindlyMD KindlyMD® is a patient-first and healthcare data company redefining value-based care and patient-centered medical services. Formed in 2019, KindlyMD leverages data analysis to deliver evidence-based, personalized solutions in order to reduce opioid use, improve health outcomes faster, and provide value based, algorithmic guidance on the use of alternative medicine in healthcare. In August 2025, KindlyMD completed its merger with Nakamoto Holdings Inc., a Bitcoin-native holding company. This strategic partnership formed a public Bitcoin strategy that unites KindlyMD’s healthcare expertise with Nakamoto’s vision of integrating Bitcoin into global capital markets, creating a diversified entity focused on both healthcare innovation and Bitcoin treasury management. About Nakamoto Nakamoto is a Bitcoin company building a global portfolio of Bitcoin-native companies. Nakamoto plans to grow its Bitcoin holdings through disciplined accumulation and to leverage its treasury to acquire and develop an ecosystem of Bitcoin companies across finance, media, advisory and more. Nakamoto aims to provide commercial and financial infrastructure for the next generation of capital markets. For more information, please visit nakamoto.com.
